system.name: NIC
system.one_liner: custom NIC hardware that maps arriving packets directly to application buffers for zero-copy DMA via per-flow memory-segment tracking

components.name: Transport Protocol Execution Environment
components.role: host control-path software that processes headers forwarded from the NIC

components.name: Application Buffers
components.role: destination memory for zero-copy DMA of payload data (e.g. CPU user space or GPU device memory)

components.name: MR
components.role: memory-region descriptor for a registered buffer

components.name: DMA
components.role: engines that copy payload to application memory and forward headers to the control path

components.name: TX Merge Unit
components.role: merges header and payload to form an outgoing packet

components.name: RX Split Unit
components.role: splits an accepted incoming packet into header and payload

components.name: MS List
components.role: list of memory segments tracking payload placement for a flow

components.name: Flow Table
components.role: tracks per-flow metadata (flow ID, flow cursor) used to index incoming packets

components.name: net port
components.role: physical network port where packets are sent and received

content.key_idea: Custom NIC hardware maps each incoming packet directly to its application buffer for zero-copy DMA by tracking per-flow memory segments (MS List) and cursors in a Flow Table, splitting/merging headers and payloads at the NIC boundary.
content.reading_order: Top-down: host-side transport stack and application/GPU buffers connect through DMA engines into the NIC's TX/RX split-merge units, which consult the Flow Table and MS List, down to the net port.

summary: This figure is a block diagram of the custom NIC hardware proposed for high-throughput, flexible host networking. Two dashed host-side boxes at the top, the Transport Protocol Execution Environment and Application Buffers (with GPU HBM and its MR descriptor as one example), connect through two DMA engines down into the solid NIC box below, illustrating a host/device split bridged by DMA. Inside the NIC, a TX Merge Unit and RX Split Unit merge or split packet headers and payloads at the net port, using blue for the sender path and red for the receiver path. A Flow Table indexes incoming packets by a header-derived tuple to find a flow's MS List, which tracks memory-segment placement so payloads can be zero-copied straight to the right application buffer; an MR Table is also linked into this per-flow bookkeeping. A boxed legend distinguishes dashed management links from solid data-path arrows.
